title: Flow Canvas preferences require 4-5 hand-wired touchpoints each; WindowState has become a 25-field pref dump with a zombie legacy field
existing_state: Adding one canvas display pref currently means: a React store field + a `layout-save` send, a hand-parsed nullable extraction in FlowCanvasForm.SavePanelSizes (UI/FlowCanvasForm.cs:447-494 — already a 15-variable if-chain with a 14-condition early-return guard at 468-472), a new `FlowCanvasXxx` property on WindowState (Models/AppConfiguration.cs:499-546 — ~25 canvas fields and counting, in a class named for window geometry), and a mirrored restore send (e.g. pref-restore at FlowCanvasForm.cs:441-444). The pattern has already produced churn: `FlowCanvasAutoReflow` (AppConfiguration.cs:535-540) is a documented zombie kept only for migration, and reduced-motion/iteration-cap travel a parallel second channel (`pref-save`, SaveReducedMotionPref at 496-508) because the first one grew awkward. A forgotten restore or a typo'd JObject key fails silently — the pref just doesn't stick, with no compile-time signal.
recommendation: Collapse the per-field plumbing: store canvas display prefs as one opaque versioned JSON object (e.g. `WindowState.FlowCanvasPrefs` as a JObject/string, or a dedicated `FlowCanvasPrefs` DTO serialized whole). React sends the full prefs object on change; C# persists it without field-by-field parsing and echoes it back verbatim on load. Field knowledge then lives in exactly one place (the React settings slice), the SavePanelSizes if-chain and pref-restore mirror disappear, and new prefs become a React-only change. Keep reading the existing 25 fields for one release to migrate.
user_benefit: New canvas settings stop being a 4-file ritual where any missed step silently loses the user's preference — the failure mode this exact code path has already exhibited (legacy AutoReflow migration, split pref channels).
